answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may influence reputation or claim rewards. A reef of independent reviewers then releases the stake only after the identity’s signal survives cross-checks against past behavior; linked accounts that copy one another can be slashed. A jetty of delayed payouts limits quick cash-outs, so an attacker must tie up more capital for longer and risks losing it when the cluster is exposed.
